inspectionQuotes.text: Pupils respond well to predictable routines.
inspectionQuotes.section: What is it like to attend this school?

inspectionStrengths.text: The focus on effective teaching for all pupils has had mixed impact to date.
inspectionStrengths.section: What does the school do well and what does it need to do better

inspectionStrengths.text: The parent who described the school as ‘going in a positive direction’ was spot on.
inspectionStrengths.section: What does the school do well and what does it need to do better

inspectionStrengths.text: The majority of pupils achieve well in reading, writing and mathematics by the end of key stage 2.
inspectionStrengths.section: What does the school do well and what does it need to do better

inspectionImprovements.text: The school needs to ensure that additional support for pupils who need it is fit for purpose and having the necessary impact.  The school is not yet realising its ambition for ‘inclusive quality-first teaching’.
inspectionImprovements.section: What does the school need to do to improve?

inspectionImprovements.text: The school must make sure that teachers are well equipped to meet the needs of all pupils in the classroom and that provision for pupils with high levels of need is appropriate.  The curriculums in their current form have only very recently been introduced.
inspectionImprovements.section: What does the school need to do to improve?

inspectionImprovements.text:  The teaching of early reading and writing is not as strong as it needs to be.
inspectionImprovements.section: What does the school need to do to improve?
